{{Short description|List of points considered center of a triangle}}
{{Use American English|date=March 2021}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=May 2025}}

The '''Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers (ETC)''' is an online list of thousands of points or "[[triangle center|centers]]" associated with the geometry of a [[triangle]]. This resource is hosted at the [[University of Evansville]]. It started from a list of 400 triangle centers published in the 1998 book ''Triangle Centers and Central Triangles'' by [[Clark Kimberling]].<ref>
{{cite book
|title=Triangle Centers and Central Triangles
|authorlink=Clark Kimberling
|series=Congressus numerantium
|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dSrSrQEACAAJ
|year=1998
|publisher=Utilitas Mathematica Publishing
}}</ref>

{{As of|2026|2|10}}, the list identifies 71,392 triangle centers<!-- one empty section exists, so don't go by the contents page --><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kimberling |first=Clark |title=Part 36: Centers X(70001) - X(72000) |url=https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/ETCPart36.html |access-date=10 Feb 2026 |website=Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers |authorlink=Clark Kimberling}}</ref> and is managed cooperatively by an international team of geometry researchers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kimberling |first=Clark |title=Thanks |url=https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/thanks.html |access-date=6 February 2024 |website=Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers |authorlink=Clark Kimberling}}</ref> The encyclopedia is integrated into [[GeoGebra|Geogebra]].<ref>{{cite web| work=Geogebra|title= TriangleCenter_Command| url=https://wiki.geogebra.org/en/TriangleCenter_Command}}</ref>

Each point in the list is identified by an index number of the form ''X''(''n'') —for example, ''X''(1) is the [[incenter]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/KimberlingCenter.html|title=Kimberling Center|author=Weisstein, Eric W.|work=MathWorld--A Wolfram Web Resource.}}</ref> The information recorded about each point includes its [[trilinear coordinates|trilinear]] and [[barycentric coordinate system (mathematics)|barycentric coordinates]] and its relation to lines joining other identified points. Links to [[The Geometer's Sketchpad]] diagrams are provided for key points.  The encyclopedia also includes a glossary of terms and definitions.

Each point in the list is assigned a distinct name. In cases where no particular name arises from geometrical or historical considerations, the name of a star is used instead.  For example, the 770th point in the list is named ''point [[Acamar]]''.

The encyclopedia is presented in parts (Part 1, Part 2, etc.). As of 12 August 2026, there are 37 Parts. In order to enable searching for names, terms, and sources across all the Parts, a [https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/Guide_to_preambles_in_ETC.html Guide to Preambles in the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers ] was made accessible in August 2026.

! ''X''(1)
| [[Incenter]]
|| center of the [[incircle and excircles of a triangle|incircle]]

|| intersection of the three [[median (geometry)|median]]s

|-
! ''X''(4)

|-
! ''X''(5)
| [[Nine-point center]]
|| center of the [[nine-point circle]]
|-
! ''X''(6)
| [[Symmedian point]]
|| intersection of the three [[symmedian]]s
|-

| [[Incircle and excircles of a triangle#Gergonne triangle and point|Gergonne point]]
|| symmedian point of contact triangle
|-
! ''X''(8)

|| intersection of lines from each vertex to the corresponding [[semiperimeter]] point
|-
! ''X''(9)

|| symmedian point of the triangle formed by the centers of the three [[incircle and excircles of a triangle|excircles]]
|-

|| center of the [[Spieker circle]]
|}

The encyclopedia also contains a list of notable bicentric pairs of points which are not by themselves triangle centers, such as the [[Brocard points]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BICENTRIC PAIRS |url=https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/BicentricPairs.html |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=faculty.evansville.edu}}</ref>

Similar, albeit shorter, lists exist for quadri-figures (quadrilaterals and systems of four lines) and polygon geometry.
